 PSG breaks Champions League record with four goals in first 17 minutes of mismatch at Villarreal
 By The Associated Press 
 November 03 2026 02:01 PM 
 PSG's Desire Doue, right, celebrates after scoring his side's second goal during the Champions League opening phase soccer match between Villarreal and Paris Saint-Germain in Villarreal, Spain, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. (AP Photo/Alberto Saiz) 
 VILLARREAL, Spain (AP) — Paris Saint-Germain faced a test of its squad strength with four of its best players missing for the trip to Villarreal in the Champions League on Tuesday.
 The defending champions were coping just fine, though.
 Helped by dreadful defending, PSG swept into a 4-0 lead after 17 minutes of a mismatch at El Madrigal — the fastest any team has reached four goals in a Champions League game, according to UEFA.
 The goals that sunk the Yellow Submarine — the nickname of Villarreal — came in an eight-minute burst, scoring in the 9th when Joao Neves poked home a loose ball after missing the initial corner into the box.
 Desire Doue added a second in the 12th, Senny Mayulu scored a minute later and Fabian Ruiz slammed home in the 17th — with all three goals stemming from mistakes by Villarreal as they played out from the back or got dispossessed in its own half.
 PSG’s Fabian Ruiz, center, celebrates after scoring his side’s third goal during the Champions League opening phase soccer match between Villarreal and Paris Saint-Germain in Villarreal, Spain, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. (AP Photo/Alberto Saiz) 
 PSG, which started the fourth round of games in first place in the standings, was without Ousmane Dembele, Marquinhos and Nuno Mendes because of thigh injuries, along with long-term absentee Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (ruptured ACL).
 It wasn’t stopping PSG heading for a 10th straight win in all competitions.
 According to UEFA, the previous fastest time a team had reached four goals in a Champions League game was 20 minutes, by Real Madrid in a 6-2 home win against Dinamo Zagreb in 2011.
 Villarreal’s manager Inigo Perez reacts during the Champions League opening phase soccer match between Villarreal and Paris Saint-Germain in Villarreal, Spain, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. (AP Photo/Alberto Saiz)
